3. Mr. A. K. M. Shafiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-petitioner has taken me through the judgments of the Courts below. Mr. Formanullah Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant opposite-parties opposes the Rule. There is no dispute about the facts of the case as stated above. The subject Matter of the suit was nal land measuring 48 satak's appertaining to a raiyati holding of mouza KuIgaon, P.S. Panchalaish, Chittagong. Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as inserted by P.O. 88 of 1972 and amended by P.O. 136 of 1972 and. P.O. 24 of 1973 reads as follows:- 

 95A. Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force; any transfer of a holding or of portion or share thereof, either way of an out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey or where The transferor receives from the transferee any Consideration and the transferee acquires the right to possess and enjoy the usufruct of such holding or Portion or share thereof for a. specified Period in lieu of such consideration, shall not withstanding anything contained in the document relating to the transfer, be deemed to be a complete mortgage for a period not exceeding seven years and the provisions of section 95 shall apply to such transfer whether made before or after the date of the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Second Amendment) Order, 1972." 

 4. In this case the transfer of the lands which are portions of a radiate holding was  made by way of out and out sale with a contemporaneous agreement, to recovery. It is clear that the transaction comes within the purview of section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and has to be treated as a Mortgage: Whether in fact it is mortgage or an out and out sale with a condition of conveyance is irrelevant. Even if the is an out and out sale with a condition of conveyance; and not a mortgage in fact, in law it is to be deemed to be complete mortgage for a period not ceding seven years. The transaction in the case before me is date 20.5.72, Section 95A was inserted in the S.A. & T. Act by the State. Acquisition and Tenancy (Second Amendment) Order 1972 (P.O. 88 Of 1972) having effect from 3.8.72. Thus on 20.5.72, the law inserting section  95A in the S.A. & T Act his not come into effect. Under the law, obtaining on 20.5.70 the transaction could not be deemed to be a mortgage in view of the provison to Clause (c); or section 58 of the Transfer Of Property Act. Even, so, however, the transaction in the instant case must be treated to be a complete usufructuary mortgage been Cause Under the newly inserted section 95A a transfer whether Made before or after the date of commencement of the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Second Intendment) Order, 1972 (P.O. 88 of 1972) is also covered. The section, because of its very language, has a retrospective effect. In interpreting Oh-section (2) of section 87 of the & T. Act inserted in the section by P.O. 137 of .1972 Which came into force on 4.11.72 and which used the words "whether before or after the 28th Jude, 1972", the appellate division in the case or Abdul Mannan and others vs. Kulada Ranjan Mawali and others reported in 31 DLR (AD) 195 has held that these words have given retrospective effected section 87, but the extent of retrospectively of the section Could not go back to any date before the provisions of Part V had come into farce. This principle Would apply to the present case also. By the words whether made before after the date of the commence Meat of the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Second Amendment) Order, 1972" a retrospective effect, has been given to section 95A, as well as to section 95, which has been referred to in section 95A, of the said Act, though such retrospectively cannot go behind any date earlier than the date, of coming into force of Part V of the Act, in which part the sections occur. The transfer in question which is of the year 1970 is however, effected by this retrospectively and has to be treated as a complete usufructuary mortgage for a period not exceeding 7 years, notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, and notwithstanding the provision of the Proviso to section 58(c) of the T.P. Act. The Appellate Division, in the case of Rania death Haji Abdul Gaul Biswas and ors reported in 32 DLR (AD) 233 has observed that plain reading of section 95A shows that any transfer of a holding by way of out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey is to be deemed to be a complete fracture mortgage and the period must not exceed seven Years that the provision of section 95 would apply for restoration or redemption. There is, therefore, no Scope for any controversy that the transaction in the present case must be treated to be complete usufructuary mortgage for a period not exceeding seven years. 

 6. Mr. Formanullah Khan submits that the remedy of the plaintiff mortgagor lay in filing an application under sub-section (4) or section 95. He could not maintain a separate suit, as done in the present case, for redemption or restoration of the mortgaged land. It is evident that this sub-section provides for Summary procedure and a speedy relief for redemption and restoration of the mortgaged property. It is too much to contend that this summitry procedure debars the mortgagor from seeing the: ordinary relief of redemption provided under the general Saw by a civil suit. The remedy of a civil suit is always available to the mortgagor. In the case of Abu Bakkar Vs. Nasir Ahmed reported in 34 DLR (AD) 237, the Appellate Division has held that the mortgagor in the case of a transaction of this nature which is deemed. to be complete usufructuary mortgage under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act may file a suit for redemption within a period of 60 years from the date of accrual of his right of redemption. 

 7. The contention of the learned Advocate Mr. Formanullah Khan that the relief of filing a suit for redemption was not available to the plaintiff-mortgagor and that the only relief was the relief provided under sub-section (4) of section. 95 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is not, therefore, tenable. The transaction took place in May 1970. Seven years elapsed in May 1977 so the cause of action for filing a suit for redemption arose in May 1977 and the plaintiff had filed the suit in 1981. Evidently there is no question of limitation. The suit is within time. On the admitted facts of this case and legal position explained above the plaintiff was entitled to a decree for redemption and restoration of possession, the mortgage having extinguished on the expiry of 7 years. The plaintiff had couched his prayer seeking relief in the suit as one for declaration that the mortgage dated 20.5.70 has been redeemed. The plaintiff however, paid ad volume Court fees and I see no difficulty in treating the suit as one for exemption proper and giving him relief on that basis.
